story.heading: The Story
paragraphs: Alanis Morissette had already released two dance-pop albums in Canada as a teenager before relocating to Los Angeles and co-writing Jagged Little Pill (1995) with producer Glen Ballard — a sharp turn toward confessional, unfiltered songwriting that became one of the best-selling albums of all time, moving over 33 million copies worldwide.

Led by 'You Oughta Know,' 'Hand In My Pocket' and 'Ironic,' Jagged Little Pill swept the 1996 Grammy Awards, winning Album of the Year and Best Rock Album. Supposed Former Infatuation Junkie (1998) followed, continuing her run of introspective songwriting into a second era.

Morissette has continued to release albums into her fourth decade, including Such Pretty Forks in the Road (2020), while Jagged Little Pill's legacy carried into a Tony-winning Broadway musical built around its songs and the 2021 HBO documentary Jagged.
She has won seven Grammy Awards from fourteen nominations across rock, pop and music-video categories.
